reason: The reading itself holds: packet.js veda 123 --verse 10.129.2 and the raw text of revision 402226 (2024-05-10, via the Wikisource API) both carry tat sakalavedāntaprasiddhaṃ brahmatattvam and svadhā māyā, tayā tad brahmaikam avibhāgāpannam āsīt, and Wilson's own (unbracketed) note agrees that Sāyaṇa takes svadhā as Māyā. verse.js ok (Rig Veda 10.129.2, at [965,2]) and entry-check ok. It fails on two lines. FORM: rule 3 allows at most three words of the key verse to be quoted, and the sentence quotes six (‘That One Thing’ and ‘its own nature’); entry-check tests only each quotation, but no one of the 202 landed teachings quotes the key twice or more than three words in all. PLAIN: the hymn does not ask what was before existent and non-existent; 10.129.1 says that then there was neither, and the questions are what covered it and (10.129.6) whence creation came, so the context clause misstates the text. The corrected sentence in better passes entry-check (44 words, scratch R5b-d123-p.json).
better: In a hymn on the time when neither non-existent nor existent was, and whence creation came, the verse tells what alone there was; Sāyaṇa, on 10.129.2, takes the One as Brahman, known throughout the Vedānta, and ‘its own nature’ as māyā, undivided from it.
